(as Angreen Photo) | hq_location = [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]], Canada | website = {{URL|astral.com}} }} '''Astral Media Inc.''' was a Canadian [[media conglomerate]]. It was Canada's largest radio broadcaster, with 84 [[radio station]]s in eight provinces. Astral was also a major player in [[premium television|premium]] and [[specialty channel|specialty]] television in Canada, with 23 specialty channels and two conventional stations. In addition, Astral had a presence in [[out-of-home advertising]]. In March 2012, [[Bell Media]] announced its intent to acquire Astral for $3.38 billion. Although an attempt to purchase the entirety of the company was blocked under [[competition law]], the [[Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission|CRTC]] approved a revised offer on June 27, 2013, which saw various Astral specialty channels and radio stations divested to competitors. The sale was consummated on July 5, 2013. Astral was dissolved later the same year as a result of Bell Media completing its acquisition of the company. Bell Media assumed some of Astral's television functions and absorbed some of its premium television services. Though defunct, the Astral name survives under its ''Astral Out-of-home'' outdoor advertising division, though it consumated the former Canadian division of [[Outfront Media]] in 2023.{{Cite news |date=October 23, 2023 |title=Bell Media signs deal to buy Canadian business of Outfront Media for $410 million |work=Toronto Star |url=https://www.thestar.com/business/bell-media-signs-deal-to-buy-outfront-medias-canadian-business-for-410-million/article_cfa549ed-3914-5d7c-bfbd-e9135a107dfd.html }} ==History== ===Angreen Photo and Astral Photo=== {{Anchor|Angreen Photo|Astral Photo}} Astral Media's roots lie with Angreen Photo, a Canadian company founded in 1961. It was created when [[Montreal]]'s Greenberg brothers,{{cite web|last=Wedge|first=Pip|title=Astral Media Inc.|url=http://www.broadcasting-history.ca/station_groups/Radio_Television_Station_Groups-Astral_Media_Inc.html|work=Radio/Television Station Group History|publisher=Canadian Communications Foundation|access-date=24 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228014833/http://www.broadcasting-history.ca/station_groups/Radio_Television_Station_Groups-Astral_Media_Inc.html|archive-date=2014-02-28|url-status=dead}} led by [[Harold Greenberg]], founded it to operate the [[photography]] concession in [[Miracle Mart]], a [[department store]] chain. Its acquisition in 1963 of Bellevue Pathé led to photography rights at the Montreal [[Expo 67]] World's Fair, and it eventually grew into a 125-store chain, [[Astral Photo]], the remnants of which are now owned by the [[Blacks Photo Corporation|Black's Photography]] chain. The company grew quickly into [[film|motion picture]] processing after acquiring the Pathé-Humphries motion picture lab in 1968 and Associated Screen News Industries of Montreal in 1969. ===Astral Communications Limited=== The company was constituted in 1973 under the name Astral Bellevue Pathé Limited. It eventually undertook [[videocassette]] duplication and video [[wholesale|wholesaling]]. The company also [[Film producer|produced]] or [[executive producer|executive produced]] over 100 feature [[film]]s, [[television program]]s and television [[miniseries]]. The films were released by [[American Cinema Productions|American Cinema Releasing]].{{cite news|title=Astral Bellevue|publisher=Globe and Mail|date=15 January 1981|id={{ProQuest|386796617}}}} The company had operated such subsidiaries as Astral Films, Astral Film Productions Ltd. and Astral Video, as well as in 1987, a development consortium that was led by [[Harold Greenberg]] with funding from the [[CBC Television|CBC]] called the Centre De Production De Montreal, which is set for open in 1989.{{Cite news |last=Brownstein |first=Bill |date=1987-07-08 |title=Greenberg's Astral Set To Build Production Center |pages=6–7 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}} In 1983, the Greenbergs acquired complete control of two [[pay television]] networks, First Choice (now known as The Movie Network) and Premier Choix TVEC (now [[Super Écran]]), at which point Astral ceased to be directly involved in [[film]] and program production. The company would later expand its television operations by launching new specialty networks. In addition, it became involved with the home video and feature film market, lasting from the mid-1980s until at least 1996. In 1987, Astral Film Enterprises had teamed up with [[Orion Pictures|Management Company Entertainment Group]] to produce three feature films by 1988, with the first film slated to be in the co-production pact was ''[[Boris and Natasha: The Movie|Boris and Natasha]]'', ''Boardwalk'', and ''Villa Golitsyn'', which were proposed in the three-picture pact, but the projects, aside from ''Boris and Natasha'' were never realized.{{Cite news |date=1987-12-02 |title=Astral, Management Co. Teaming On 3 Features; 'Boris & Natasha' First |page=6 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}} In 1996, Astral Communications decided to sell all of the program development and distribution divisions to [[TVA Films|Coscient Group]].{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Brendan |date=1996-12-19 |title=Astral reports $10.7 mil loss, ups Bureau to chair |url=https://variety.com/1996/scene/vpage/astral-reports-10-7-mil-loss-ups-bureau-to-chair-1117466584/ |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=Variety |language=en-US}} In February 2000, Astral Communications changed its name to Astral Media. [[File:Astralmedia.svg|thumb|Astral's "Uppercase A with circle cut" Logo from 2000 to 2010, using the full company name.]] Astral then expanded into radio, beginning with the 2000 acquisition of Radiomutuel, and the 2002 purchase of most of the radio assets of [[Telemedia]], although those companies' joint AM radio network [[Radiomedia]] was ultimately sold to [[Corus Entertainment]] for competitive reasons. Radiomutuel also owned a controlling share of [[outdoor advertising]] firm Omni Outdoor (which eventually became the fully owned Astral Out-of-Home division), as well as several French-language specialty channels such as [[Canal Vie]], [[Z (TV channel)|Ztélé]], [[Séries+]], [[Vrak|VRAK.TV]], and 50% stakes in [[Elle Fictions|MusiquePlus]] and [[Max (Canadian TV channel)|MusiMax]] (then co-owned with [[CHUM Limited]]). On February 23, 2007, Astral Media announced that it had signed a letter of intent and had entered into exclusive negotiations regarding the acquisition of "substantially all of the assets" of [[Standard Broadcasting|Standard Radio]].[http://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/February2007/23/c3982.html Astral Media announces signature of letter of intent to acquire Standard Radio] A formal agreement was later announced, with the proposed transaction being approved by the [[Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission|CRTC]] on September 28, and completed on October 29 of the same year. The transaction gave Astral Media a significant foothold in English-language radio. [[File:AstralMediaVehicle.JPG|thumb|Astral vehicle with the 2010 logo]] In 2010, Astral Media relocated its headquarters to 1800 [[McGill College Avenue]], in a skyscraper rechristened [[Maison Astral]]. In May 2010, the company unveiled a new logo featuring a multi-coloured "a" insignia (reflecting ideals of "collaboration" and "creativity"). At this time, the company began to trade as simply "Astral".{{Cite web|url=http://marketingmag.ca/media/astral-media-rebrand-for-consistency-2870|title=Astral Media rebrand for consistency|last=Lloyd|first=Jeromy|website=Marketing Magazine|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-04}} In the fall of 2011, [[Cartoon Network (Canada)|Teletoon]] (co-owned with [[Corus Entertainment]] at the time) adopted a new logo to reflect Astral's 50th anniversary. ===Acquisition by Bell Media=== On March 16, 2012, Astral Media announced that it had agreed to be acquired by [[Bell Canada]] through its [[Bell Media]] division for $3.38 billion. Astral Media shareholders approved the acquisition of all of its issued and outstanding shares by Bell Media on May 24, 2012;[http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-shareholders-approve-acquisition-by-bce/1001407600/ Astral Shareholders Approve Acquisition by BCE] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808045557/http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-shareholders-approve-acquisition-by-bce/1001407600/ |date=2014-08-08 }}, ''Broadcaster Magazine'', May 24, 2012. the acquisition of Astral Media's issued and outstanding shares by Bell received approval by the [[Quebec Superior Court]] during a hearing on May 25, 2012.[http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-receives-final-court-approval-for-acquisition-by-bce/1001410098/ BCE shuts down Astral Media for $3.38 billion] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808043752/http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-receives-final-court-approval-for-acquisition-by-bce/1001410098/ |date=2014-08-08 }}, ''Broadcaster Magazine'', May 25, 2012. The proposed sale faced opposition: a coalition of [[Cogeco]], [[Vidéotron]], and [[EastLink (company)|Eastlink]] argued that Bell's market share following the merger would harm [[consumer choice]], and that Bell would raise carriage fees for Astral's channels (impacting smaller providers).{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Julia|title=Cable company opposition to Bell's Astral purchase heats up|url=http://business.financialpost.com/2012/08/07/cable-company-opposition-to-bells-astral-purchase-heats-up/|publisher=Financial Post|access-date=19 September 2012}} During a CRTC's hearing, the [[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] argued that Bell's proposal to use its mandatory tangible benefits to launch a French-language news channel (which would compete with its own [[Réseau de l'information]]) was "self-serving and unprecedented."{{cite news|title=CBC challenges BCE-Astral deal|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/cbc-challenges-bce-astral-deal/article4545447/|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=2 October 2012|location=Toronto|date=14 September 2012}} In September 2012, the [[Competition Bureau (Canada)|Competition Bureau]] stated that it was becoming "increasingly concerned" about the implications of the merger, and warned that it could oppose the deal even if it were to be approved by the CRTC.{{cite news|title=Competition Bureau flags Bell-Astral deal|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/competition-bureau-flags-bell-astral-deal/article4548430/|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=19 September 2012|location=Toronto|date=17 September 2012}} On October 18, 2012, the CRTC announced that it had rejected BCE's proposal to acquire Astral Media. The commission cited that their combined market power could "threaten the availability of diverse programming for Canadians and endanger the ability of distribution undertakings to deliver programming at affordable rates and on reasonable terms on multiple platforms", and also stated that allowing the merger would have required the implementation of "extensive and intrusive safeguards" across the entire broadcasting industry. The CRTC also felt that Bell did not adequately demonstrate how having most of Canada's French-language media owned by two vertically integrated companies would improve competition, and how being bigger would allow it to compete against foreign services.{{cite web|title=Broadcasting Decision CRTC 2012-574|url=http://crtc.gc.ca/eng/archive/2012/2012-574.htm|publisher=CRTC|access-date=18 October 2012}} ====Second attempt==== Following the rejection of the deal by the CRTC, Bell Canada CEO [[George A. Cope]] asserted that calling the merger dead was "premature", citing that the formal merger agreement between Bell and Astral did not expire until December 16, 2012, and either company could extend it to January 15, 2013. Bell attempted to ask the [[Cabinet of Canada|Cabinet]] to overturn the CRTC's decision, but was told that they did not have the ability to do so. Bell also reportedly considered going to the [[Federal Court of Appeal (Canada)|Federal Court of Appeal]], or restructuring the deal to selectively sell Astral assets to competing companies. [[Rogers Media]] expressed interest in acquiring some of Astral's channels if such a sale were to occur.{{cite news|title=With Astral deal on ropes, BCE keeps its options open|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/with-astral-deal-on-ropes-bce-keeps-its-options-open/article4809262/|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=3 November 2012|location=Toronto|date=1 November 2012}}{{cite news|title=As Astral posts gains, Greenberg looks to rescue BCE deal|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/as-astral-posts-gains-greenberg-looks-to-rescue-bce-deal/article4790099/|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=3 November 2012|location=Toronto|date=31 October 2012}} On November 16, 2012, Astral confirmed that it was in talks with Bell to negotiate a new offer, which would involve the sale of the majority of its English-language television channels to third parties.{{cite news|title=Astral confirms talks with BCE to resurrect takeover deal|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/astral-confirms-talks-with-bce-to-resurrect-takeover-deal/article5369161/|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=17 November 2012|location=Toronto|date=16 November 2012}} On March 4, 2013, the [[Competition Bureau]] approved a new proposal by Bell to acquire Astral Media, which would involve the divestiture of certain television channels and radio stations owned by the combined company, and was subject to restrictions preventing Bell from imposing restrictive bundling requirements on any provider seeking to carry The Movie Network or [[Super Écran]].{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/bce-to-sell-assets-to-corus-as-part-of-astral-deal/article9272784/|title=Bell moves closer to Astral with sale of TV assets|date=4 March 2013|access-date=5 March 2013|publisher=The Globe and Mail|location=Toronto}} The CRTC made the proposed takeover proposal public on March 6, 2013.[http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-and-bell-comment-on-new-acquisition-application-to-crtc/1002122078/ Astral and Bell Comment on New Acquisition Application to CRTC] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002110735/http://www.broadcastermagazine.com/news/astral-and-bell-comment-on-new-acquisition-application-to-crtc/1002122078/ |date=2015-10-02 }}, ''Broadcaster Magazine'', March 6, 2013. Unlike the previous deal, which would have given Bell a 42% share of the English-language television market, the new deal gave Bell a total market share of 35.7%, and increased its French-language market share to 22% (in comparison to 8% before).{{cite news|title=Competition Bureau OK's BCE-Astral deal, with conditions|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/competition-bureau-ok-s-bce-astral-deal-with-conditions-1.1326790|publisher=CBC News|access-date=5 March 2013}} On March 18, 2013, the Competition Bureau cleared a proposed deal to sell Astral's stakes in several channels to [[Corus Entertainment]] in preparation for regulatory approval.{{cite news|title=Competition Bureau clears Corus acquisition of Astral assets|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/competition-bureau-clears-corus-acquisition-of-astral-assets/article9886090/|work=The Globe and Mail|publisher=Canadian Press|access-date=20 March 2013|location=Toronto|date=18 March 2013}} In a speech to the [[Academy of Canadian Cinema and Television]] prior to the hearings, Bell Media's president Kevin Crull detailed plans to invest in French-language productions and maintain a distinct operation in Montreal devoted to its French-language outlets. Crull also praised the role of [[Québecor Média]] (despite the company being opposed to the merger) in using its own [[vertical integration]] strategy to help promote Francophone talent, and revealed his intention to try and emulate its "star system" in English Canada.{{cite web|title=Bell wants to duplicate Quebec's star system in English Canada |url=https://montrealgazette.com/business/Bell+Media+wants+duplicate+Quebec+star+system+English+Canada/8301826/story.html |publisher=Montreal Gazette |access-date=8 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622073255/http://www.montrealgazette.com/business/Bell%2BMedia%2Bwants%2Bduplicate%2BQuebec%2Bstar%2Bsystem%2BEnglish%2BCanada/8301826/story.html |archive-date=22 June 2013 }} =====Hearings and approval===== CRTC hearings on the new proposals began in May 2013. Asserting that it would have to sell or shut down the station without one, Bell organized a petition proposing an exception to the ownership cap that would allow it to maintain ownership of [[CKGM]], under the condition that Bell maintain the TSN Radio format on the station and provide $245,000 in funding for local [[amateur sports]] and [[scholarship]]s in sports journalism over a seven-year period. Commissioner Suzanne Lamarre commented that Bell could have sold another station instead, given most of the comments on Bell's petition only supported CKGM maintaining a [[sports radio]] format, and not Bell's purchase of Astral. In response, Bell's CEO [[George A. Cope]] commented that the company did not want to sell off profitable radio stations, and Astral CEO Jacques Parisien remarked that breaking up its Montreal cluster would affect their operation.{{cite web|title=Bell resistant to CRTC's TSN 690 proposal |url=https://montrealgazette.com/business/Bell+shoots+down+idea+selling+profitable+radio+station+keep/8345313/story.html |publisher=Montreal Gazette |access-date=8 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130508232611/http://www.montrealgazette.com/business/Bell%2Bshoots%2Bdown%2Bidea%2Bselling%2Bprofitable%2Bradio%2Bstation%2Bkeep/8345313/story.html |archive-date=8 May 2013 }} Rogers called on the CRTC to require that Bell divest The Movie Network, claiming that Bell would make it harder and more expensive for competing service providers to access The Movie Network's content (especially on its own Anyplace TV and on-demand services) if Bell were to own the service. Bell disputed Rogers' claims, stating that the company already had a long-term deal to distribute The Movie Network on its cablesystems, and noted that Rogers had expressed interest in purchasing the service if it were to be divested.{{cite news|title=Rogers seeks order that Bell sell Movie Network if Astral takeover is allowed|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/rogers-seeks-order-that-bell-sell-movie-network-if-astral-takeover-is-allowed-1.1354297|publisher=Canadian Press|access-date=8 May 2013}} Bell indicated that it would not go ahead with the deal if it were forced by the CRTC to sell additional media outlets.{{cite news|title=Bell won't sell more of Astral's assets to win OK for merger|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bell-won-t-sell-more-of-astral-s-assets-to-win-ok-for-merger-1.1355755|publisher=Canadian Press|access-date=22 May 2013}} Rogers also showed interest in making a "reasonable offer" to purchase CKGM as a complement to its recently acquired TV station [[CJNT-DT]]. Under Rogers ownership, CKGM would have kept its sports talk format, but as a [[Sportsnet Radio]] station instead of TSN Radio.{{cite web|title=Rogers tells CRTC it is willing to buy TSN 690 |url=https://montrealgazette.com/business/Rogers+tells+CRTC+willing/8396395/story.html |work=The Gazette |access-date=11 June 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704145756/http://www.montrealgazette.com/business/Rogers%2Btells%2BCRTC%2Bwilling/8396395/story.html |archive-date=4 July 2013 }} On June 27, 2013, the CRTC approved Bell's acquisition of Astral Media, which closed on July 5, 2013. The deal was subject to conditions, including the requirement for Bell to provide fair treatment to its competitors, to not impose "restrictive bundling practices" on Astral's premium movie channels, invest $246.9 million over the next seven years on Canadian-produced programming, and to maintain the operation and local programming levels of all of its television stations through 2017. The CRTC also approved Bell's proposed exemptions for maintaining ownership of CKGM.{{cite news|title=CRTC approves Bell/Astral deal with conditions|url=https://www.thestar.com/business/tech_news/2013/06/27/crtc_approves_bellastral_deal_with_conditions.html|work=Toronto Star|access-date=5 July 2013|date=27 June 2013}}{{cite news|title=CRTC approves Bell-Astral merger|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/crtc-approves-bell-astral-merger-1.1367433|work=CBC News|access-date=5 July 2013}} ===== Divestments ===== Following the approval of the new proposal by the Competition Bureau, [[Corus Entertainment]] reached a tentative deal to acquire 2 radio stations ([[CJOT-FM|CJOT]], [[CKQB-FM|CKQB]]), along with Astral's stakes in [[Historia (TV channel)|Historia]], [[SériesPlus|Séries+]], and the [[Cartoon Network (Canada)|Teletoon]] networks from Bell for just over $400 million. Corus acquired the stakes in Historia and Séries+ from [[Shaw Media]] as well. On January 1, 2014, the acquisition was completed. In 2017, Corus attempted to sell Historia and Séries+ to Bell for $200 million, but the deal was blocked and rejected by the Competition Bureau for violations of conditions forbidding Bell from re-acquiring divested Astral properties for ten years.{{Cite news|url=http://business.financialpost.com/telecom/media/analysts-predict-steeper-corus-dividend-cut-after-watchdog-blocks-200-million-sale-of-tv-stations-to-bell|title=Analysts predict steeper Corus dividend cut after watchdog blocks $200-million sale of TV stations to Bell|date=2018-05-28|work=Financial Post|access-date=2018-05-28|language=en-US}} Bell Media also divested [[Family Channel (Canada)|Family]], Disney Junior's [[Family Jr.|English]] and [[Télémagino|French]] services, [[WildBrainTV|Disney XD]], [[Max (Canadian TV channel)|MusiMax]], [[Elle Fictions|MusiquePlus]], and 5 other radio stations in [[Toronto]] and [[Vancouver]] ([[CHBM-FM]], [[CFXJ-FM]], [[CKZZ-FM]], [[CHLG-FM|CHHR-FM]] and [[CISL (AM)|CISL]]) at auction. These divested stations and channels were temporarily held in a [[blind trust]] by [[Pierre Boivin]] until the completion of their acquisitions.{{cite web|last=Biblic|first=Mirko|title=Re: Voting Trust Agreement between BCE Inc. and Pierre Boivin, the trustee Application No. 2013-0243-9 – Approved|url=http://www.crtc.gc.ca/eng/archive/2013/lb130627.htm|publisher=CRTC|access-date=5 July 2013}} On May 16, 2013, the [[Jim Pattison Group]] announced a deal to acquire three stations in Calgary and Winnipeg from Bell and Astral—[[CKCE-FM]], [[CHIQ-FM]], and [[CFQX]], for an undisclosed amount. The deal expanded the Jim Pattison Group's operations in Calgary (where it was planning to launch a new station, [[CKWD-FM|CHPK-FM]]), and gave the company its first stations in Manitoba.{{cite web|title=Pattison group looks to buy castoffs from Bell Astral deal|url=https://vancouversun.com/business/Pattison+group+looks+castoffs+from+Bell+Astral+deal/8399588/story.html|publisher=The Vancouver Sun|access-date=22 May 2013}}{{Dead link|date=February 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On August 26, 2013, [[Stingray Radio|Newcap Radio]] announced its intent to acquire the five aforementioned Toronto and Vancouver stations.{{cite web|url=http://www.newswire.ca/en/story/1215153/newcap-signs-agreement-with-bell-media-to-acquire-five-radio-stations-in-toronto-and-vancouver|title=Newcap signs agreement with Bell Media to acquire five radio stations in Toronto and Vancouver|publisher=CNW|access-date=26 August 2013}} Eventually, Newcap was in turn acquired by [[Stingray Group|Stingray Digital Group]] in 2018. On November 28, 2013, [[WildBrain|DHX Media]] announced that it had reached a deal to acquire Family Channel and its sister networks for $170 million, the deal was completed in late July 2014.{{cite news|title=DHX Media to buy Family, other children's channels|url=https://www.thestar.com/business/2013/11/28/dhx_media_to_buy_family_other_childrens_channels.html|work=Toronto Star|access-date=29 November 2013|date=28 November 2013}}{{cite news|title=DHX to acquire Family Channel, three others from Bell Media|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/dhx-to-acquire-family-channel-others-from-bell-media/article15648767/|work=The Globe and Mail|access-date=29 November 2013|location=Toronto|date=28 November 2013}} On December 4, 2013, [[Remstar Media Group|Remstar]], owners of the French television system [[Noovo|V]], announced that it would acquire MusiquePlus and MusiMax for an undisclosed amount.{{cite web|title=Bell Media signs deal to sell MusiquePlus and MusiMax to V Media Group|url=https://montrealgazette.com/business/Bell+Media+signs+deal+sell+MusiquePlus+MusiMax+Media+Group/9242635/story.html|work=Canadian Press|access-date=4 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211201310/http://www.montrealgazette.com/business/Bell+Media+signs+deal+sell+MusiquePlus+MusiMax+Media+Group/9242635/story.html|archive-date=2013-12-11|url-status=dead}} ==Corporate governance== Members of the [[board of directors]] of Astral prior to the close of the Bell-Astral transaction were: Austin Beutel, Paul Bronfman, [[André Bureau]] (chairman), Jack Cockwell, [[George Cohon]], [[Paul Godfrey]], Stephen Greenberg, [[Ian Greenberg]], Sidney Greenberg, Sidney Horn, Timothy Price, Phyllis Yaffe and [[Monique Jérôme-Forget]]. ==Former assets== Any listing with a cross (†) character at the end indicates an asset which was not acquired by Bell Canada. ===Radio=== ====Alberta==== * [[Calgary]] - Astral Media Inc. was a Canadian media conglomerate. It was Canada's largest radio broadcaster, with 84 radio stations in eight provinces. Astral was also a major player in premium and specialty television in Canada, with 23 specialty channels and two conventional stations. In addition, Astral had a presence in out-of-home advertising.
In March 2012, Bell Media announced its intent to acquire Astral for $3.38 billion. Although an attempt to purchase the entirety of the company was blocked under competition law, the CRTC approved a revised offer on June 27, 2013, which saw various Astral specialty channels and radio stations divested to competitors. The sale was consummated on July 5, 2013. Astral was dissolved later the same year as a result of Bell Media completing its acquisition of the company. Bell Media assumed some of Astral's television functions and absorbed some of its premium television services.
Though defunct, the Astral name survives under its Astral Out-of-home outdoor advertising division, though it consumated the former Canadian division of Outfront Media in 2023.
